title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
prompt: Given a string `s` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest substring that contains at most `k` distinct characters.

examples.explanation: The substring "ece" has length 3 with 2 distinct characters, 'e' and 'c'.
The substring "aa" has length 2 with 1 distinct character.
With k = 0, no substring can contain any characters, so the longest valid substring is empty

hints: This generalizes the 'at most 2 distinct characters' problem — the same sliding window idea works for any k.
Use a sliding window with a hash map counting occurrences of each character currently inside it.

Expand the window to the right; whenever the map has more than k distinct keys, shrink from the left (decrementing counts, deleting a key once it hits zero) until at most k remain, tracking the max window length seen. Handle k = 0 as a special case with answer 0.

solution.approach: Maintain a sliding window with a hash map from character to its count inside the window. Expand the window by moving right and updating the map. Whenever the map holds more than k distinct characters, shrink from the left, decrementing the count of the character leaving and removing it from the map entirely once its count reaches zero, until at most k distinct characters remain. Track the maximum window length seen; if k is 0, no non-empty window can qualify, so the answer is 0.
